title: Off-chain distribution signatures on the vault's typed data, configured keys, operations-trigger role, degraded-return gate
goal: Close red-team findings RT-R58-02, RT-R58-03 and RT-R58-04 off-chain, matching the WP-38 contract change. (1) The distribution signer and the verifier sign the vault's EIP-712 PayoutAuthorization typed data with secp256k1 keys through the injected signer clients (roles distribution-signer and verifier from packages/adapters/src/signing), so the same two signatures gate the manifest off-chain and the vault on-chain; the Ed25519 fixture scheme stays only under the fixture evidence profile. (2) packages/runner/src/distribution/manifest.mjs must take the two public identities from configuration (the addresses pinned in bindings/robinhood-chain.json or the operator configuration) under the production profile; the hardcoded keys whose private counterparts live in test fixtures are used only by the fixture profile and never accepted in production. (3) Add the operations-trigger EVM signer role to packages/adapters/src/signing (a second EVM key distinct from the authorizer) and use it in the stages that PegCycleVault requires the trigger to call (executeOutbound and the return leg), so a live cycle can actually complete. (4) recordDegradedReturn with acceptDegraded true is only sent when a standing-authority scoped owner authorization for that exact cycle is present (through StandingAuthorityProvider), never on the worker's own decision; the dashboard exposes it as an explicit owner action.
writeSet: docs/modules/index.json (only the sha256 entries of existing registered cards among these)
readSet: docs/modules/peg-cycle-vault.md as updated by WP-38 (typed-data schema, domain, pinned addresses)
steps: Implement the EIP-712 encoding of PayoutAuthorization in packages/runner (dependency-free keccak is available through the existing digest helpers or node:crypto; if keccak-256 is not available in the runner core, put the encoder in packages/adapters and pass the digest in) and a cross-check test against a Foundry-produced vector for the same struct (cast or a Forge test that prints the digest)

distribution-signer.mjs: production profile signs the typed-data digest through the injected signer client (secp256k1) and verifies with address recovery; fixture profile unchanged; manifest.mjs takes the two addresses from configuration in production and refuses the fixture identities there

Add the operations-trigger role; environment.mjs loads it as a second EVM signer; outbound.mjs and return.mjs call the trigger-gated vault functions with it; funding.mjs and payout.mjs keep the authorizer; compose refuses to start live mode when the two EVM identities are equal
hook-contract-client.mjs: authorizePayout calldata carries the two signatures; payout.mjs passes the signer approval and the verifier receipt signatures through

Degraded return: distribution or return stage sends recordDegradedReturn with acceptDegraded true only with a matching StandingAuthorityProvider authorization for that cycle; dashboard decision accept-degraded-return records the owner action and its authorization reference

Tests: two-signature round trip against the Foundry vector; production profile rejects fixture identities; live cycle with two EVM signers completes in compose.test.mjs; single EVM identity refuses to start; degraded acceptance without authorization is refused; run all suites and the scanner before the single commit
tests: cd packages/adapters && npm ci --ignore-scripts && node --test test/**/*.test.mjs
acceptance: The off-chain approval and verification signatures are the same EIP-712 signatures the vault verifies, proven against a Foundry-produced digest vector
Under the production profile the fixture identities are rejected and the two addresses come from configuration
A live cycle with distinct authorizer and operations-trigger identities completes; a single shared identity refuses to start live mode
acceptDegraded is impossible without a scoped owner authorization
All suites green; clean-room scanner green; packages/runner and packages/dashboard keep zero npm dependencies
notes: R4: fresh-context reviewer mandatory. No code path may read key material; signing is only through the injected signer clients. Keep gates/init.json untouched. This package depends on WP-38 being merged first; read its card and interface before coding.
